commit_message:
[HIP] Keep allocation completion ordered with its signal stream (#25291)

Queue allocations run on the async memory stream and record their
signal-semaphore events there. The cleanup event that advances those
semaphores on the host, however, was always recorded on the dispatch
stream. Allocation completion was therefore observed independently of
the stream that performed it.

`iree_hal_hip_device_stream_add_cleanup` now records on the stream it is
given, and semaphore signalling passes the stream its events were
recorded on. Queue reads and submissions keep using the dispatch stream.

Assisted-by: Codex

commit_message:
[CI] Publish OpenSSF Scorecard results and add the badge

The weekly OpenSSF Scorecard scan still files IREE under the old
repository names, so there are no results for github.com/iree-org/iree
and no badge can point at them.

Run the Scorecard action weekly with `publish_results: true`. This
publishes the results under iree-org/iree, replaces the weekly scan's
results for the repository, and uploads the SARIF report to code
scanning. The job follows the workflow restrictions the Scorecard API
enforces before it accepts published results.

Add the Scorecard badge next to the OpenSSF Best Practices badge. It
shows a score once the first run has published results.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
Add opt-in promotion of large allocas to scratch memory

Add iree-llvmcpu-promote-large-allocas, which moves the largest static
entry-block memref.alloca ops to #iree_codegen.workgroup_local memory until
the remaining stack usage fits within the configured stack allocation limit.
These allocations are then packed by iree-llvmcpu-assign-workgroup-local-memory
into runtime-provided HAL workgroup local (scratch) memory instead of the stack.

The promotion is off by default and enabled with
--iree-llvmcpu-promote-allocas-to-scratch-memory. The stack size accounting
used by iree-llvmcpu-check-ir-before-llvm-conversion is moved unchanged into
getStackAllocationLimit/getStackAllocationSize helpers so both passes share it.

Assisted-by: GitHub Copilot
Signed-off-by: Cyril Six <csix@kalrayinc.com>

commit_message:
Add opt-in promotion of large allocas to scratch memory

Add iree-llvmcpu-promote-large-allocas, which moves the largest static
entry-block memref.alloca ops to #iree_codegen.workgroup_local memory until
the remaining stack usage fits within the configured stack allocation limit.
These allocations are then packed by iree-llvmcpu-assign-workgroup-local-memory
into runtime-provided HAL workgroup local (scratch) memory instead of the stack.

The promotion is off by default and enabled with
--iree-llvmcpu-promote-allocas-to-scratch-memory. The stack size accounting
used by iree-llvmcpu-check-ir-before-llvm-conversion is moved unchanged into
getStackAllocationLimit/getStackAllocationSize helpers so both passes share it.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Honor --iree-llvmcpu-skip-intermediate-roundings=false for RVV Zvfhmin f16 inner_tiled MMA (#25125)

Zvfhmin lacks native f16 MAC, so f16 MMA widens accumulator to f32
then truncates back. These extf/truncf pairs were marked as invertible
and hoisted out of K loop, dropping per-K rounding and producing wrong
answers. The skip-intermediate-roundings flag was not plumbed into
lowering at all.

Propagate skipIntermediateRoundings through inner tile lowering and the
LLVMCPU vector pipelines. When we need to preserve roundings
(widenF16Acc
&& !skipIntermediateRoundings), materialize the f16 -> f32 -> f16
round-trip directly around each MA step in emitIntrinsic, and drop the
hoistable distribute/reassemble accumulator pair.

Add tests covering both keep-rounding and skip-rounding modes.

Fixes: https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/25058
Assisted-by: Claude Code, Doubao, DeepSeek

Signed-off-by: Yalong <yalong@multicorewareinc.com>

commit_message:
[HIP] Keep allocation completion ordered with its signal stream (#25291)

Queue allocations run on the async memory stream and record their
signal-semaphore events there. The cleanup event that advances those
semaphores on the host, however, was always recorded on the dispatch
stream. Allocation completion was therefore observed independently of
the stream that performed it.

`iree_hal_hip_device_stream_add_cleanup` now records on the stream it is
given, and semaphore signalling passes the stream its events were
recorded on. Queue reads and submissions keep using the dispatch stream.

Assisted-by: Codex

commit_message:
Add opt-in promotion of large allocas to scratch memory

Add iree-llvmcpu-promote-large-allocas, which moves the largest static
entry-block memref.alloca ops to #iree_codegen.workgroup_local memory until
the remaining stack usage fits within the configured stack allocation limit.
These allocations are then packed by iree-llvmcpu-assign-workgroup-local-memory
into runtime-provided HAL workgroup local (scratch) memory instead of the stack.

The promotion is off by default and enabled with
--iree-llvmcpu-promote-allocas-to-scratch-memory. The stack size accounting
used by iree-llvmcpu-check-ir-before-llvm-conversion is moved unchanged into
getStackAllocationLimit/getStackAllocationSize helpers so both passes share it.

[CI] Publish OpenSSF Scorecard results and add the badge

repository names, so there are no results for github.com/iree-org/iree
and no badge can point at them.

Run the Scorecard action weekly with `publish_results: true`. This
publishes the results under iree-org/iree, replaces the weekly scan's
results for the repository, and uploads the SARIF report to code
scanning. The job follows the workflow restrictions the Scorecard API
enforces before it accepts published results.

Add the Scorecard badge next to the OpenSSF Best Practices badge. It
shows a score once the first run has published results.

The weekly OpenSSF Scorecard scan still files IREE under the old
repository names, so there are no results for github.com/iree-org/iree
and no badge can point at them.

Run the Scorecard action weekly with `publish_results: true`. This
publishes the results under iree-org/iree, replaces the weekly scan's
results for the repository, and uploads the SARIF report to code
scanning. The job follows the workflow restrictions the Scorecard API
enforces before it accepts published results.

Add the Scorecard badge next to the OpenSSF Best Practices badge. It
shows a score once the first run has published results.

Assisted-by: Claude Code
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
